title: Add shortcuts for new instance and reverse cycling of taskmanager entries
line: Meta+Ctrl+number now cycles a Task Manager entry's windows backward, and each entry gets an assignable "Open New Window" shortcut.
explanation: The Task Manager registered only "Activate Task Manager Entry N" shortcuts (Meta+1..9, plus next/previous task across all entries since 6.8), so there was no way to cycle one entry's grouped windows in reverse or to open a new window of an entry from the keyboard. The change adds two per-entry global actions to the applet backend: "Cycle Backward Through Task Manager Entry N" (default Meta+Ctrl+N), which runs the same group cycling as Meta+N in the opposite direction, and "Open New Window of Task Manager Entry N", which calls the same requestNewInstance as Shift+click or middle-click. Both are dispatched to the same panel as the existing Meta+N shortcuts.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: add backward cycling and new window shortcuts

The Meta+number shortcuts could only activate an entry or cycle through
its group's windows forward. This adds per-entry actions that cycle the
group backward (Meta+Ctrl+number) and open a new window of the entry.

BUG: 464321

media.caption: Master: Meta+1 cycles the Konsole group forward; Meta+Ctrl+1 and Meta+Shift+1 do nothing.
Fixed: Meta+Ctrl+1 steps back through the Konsole windows (usr, var, etc, usr), and the new-window action, bound to Meta+Shift+1, opens a fourth Konsole.
